item.title: Why I rejected European country posting for South Africa — Fani-Kayode
item.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed that he appealed to President Bola Tinubu to be reassigned to South Africa after he was initially posted to a European country. He made the disclosure at a dinner and reception organised by the Nigerian High Commission and Consular Office in Pretoria following the presentation of his letters of credence to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on November 13. “I was sent here by our president, President Bola Ahmed, president of the Federal Republic of Nigeria — 250 million strong, a massive country, resilient people with rich history, very proud people, hard-working people that love life and love their country passionately, and I’ve been sent to represent those people and our government in a country which is equally resilient, hard-working, decent, civilised, with an equally rich history and heritage, as we have,” he said. Explaining his choice of South Africa, the envoy said the two countries could work together to advance the interests of the continent. “And that’s why I chose this country. I was initially posted to a European country, and I made an appeal to our president that I preferred to go to South Africa, which he graciously agreed to. So I find myself here,” he added. Fani-Kayode was initially posted as Nigeria’s ambassador to Germany before he was reassigned to South Africa in May. At the time, he said he had formally approached the then Minister of Foreign Affairs, Yusuf Tuggar, to express his reservations about the Germany posting. The former minister said he was uncomfortable with the appointment for “a number of personal reasons” and because he had spent most of his life in Europe. He also said he preferred South Africa, a country he had never visited but had considerable interest in. Ita Enang, who was initially posted to South Africa, was subsequently reassigned to Germany in Fani-Kayode’s place. Speaking about his priorities in South Africa, Fani-Kayode said he had begun addressing issues affecting Nigerians in the country since his arrival. He also described those behind xenophobic attacks as a “tiny minority”, arguing that they did not represent the majority of South Africans, whom he described as decent and accommodating. item.title: Xi, Trump and Putin begin unprecedented summit in China
item.description: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia kicked off their first trilateral talks on Thursday, aimed according to Beijing as “safeguarding world peace” but sparking alarm and derision elsewhere. The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, which analysts expect to be heavier in symbolism than breakthroughs, comes with Russia’s Ukraine offensive approaching the five-year mark. Trump is bogged down by his war with Iran that has choked oil supplies and pushed up consumer prices worldwide, while an ascendant China is looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. The Kylin Villa summit has stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”, who responded in English: “Nice to meet you.” Trump and Xi then came together — for the third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting their “very special relationship”. The two men’s talks were expected to touch on trade and potentially common rules for artificial intelligence, under the cloud of the Nvidia spy scandal. “During this period, China-US relations have remained generally stable and improved, bringing tangible benefits to the people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world,” Xi said. Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said. Beijing, Washington and Moscow have given different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. Trump said in his meeting with Xi however that both China and the United States were “looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine.” The Kremlin has said that the agenda had not been finalised, but it would be hard to avoid discussing Ukraine at the meeting, which is set to last “no more than an hour”. Germany was also due to host Ukraine’s allies for a “Coalition of the Willing” meeting on Thursday involving envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. China has said only that the trio will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting will be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin. item.title: Learn to grow; stop running your mouth all over – Lamido tells Shettima
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎Former Jigawa State Governor and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) founding member, Dr Sule Lamido, has called on Vice President Kashim Shettima to exercise greater caution in his public comments, urging him to demonstrate the maturity and seriousness expected of someone holding such a high office. ‎Lamido made the remarks while speaking with journalists shortly after the PDP campaign flag-off in Dutse on Wednesday. ‎He acknowledged Shettima’s intelligence, eloquence and personal qualities but argued that effective leadership requires more than these attributes. According to him, the Vice President must recognise the importance of his position and appreciate the responsibility that comes with being the country’s second-highest political office holder and a leading figure in Northern Nigeria. ‎”Let him understand that he is number one in the North. Whatever he says must be taken seriously. He needs to move away from jokes because I think he does not fully appreciate the responsibilities attached to the office he occupies,” Lamido said. He further challenged Shettima to use his position to advance the interests of Northern Nigeria rather than engage in public exchanges that could undermine the dignity of his office. ‎Lamido also expressed displeasure over some of the Vice President’s previous remarks about prominent political figures, including former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Senate President Ahmad Lawan. He recalled that Shettima had previously referred to Osinbajo as an ice-cream seller and Atiku as a sanitation inspector, describing such remarks as disrespectful to individuals who had occupied important positions in the country. ‎The former governor maintained that Shettima should be more conscious of how his statements are received and interpreted by the public. ‎”He needs to be more serious and go beyond making jokes. He should consider what he says, how people perceive him and the meaning they attach to his statements instead of speaking carelessly,” he said. Lamido stressed that the Vice Presidency demands a high level of responsibility and decorum, urging Shettima to improve his conduct and demonstrate greater respect for the institution he represents. ‎He added that the position carries responsibilities that should not be treated lightly, insisting that the Vice President must rise to the expectations of his office. ‎Speaking at the event , Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chairman in Jigawa State Hon. Babandi Ibrahim Gumel says the momouth crowd shows the people of the state are tired with the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and are ready to votes it out coming 2027 governorship election, insisting that incumbency will not guarantee its victory. ‎The party said the growing dissatisfaction among residents over their current condition would pave the way for the PDP’s return to power in the state. item.title: Musk says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ for failed US election spending
item.description: World’s richest man Elon Musk said Wednesday he felt “pretty foolish” for donating nearly half a billion dollars to failed campaigns in recent US midterm elections, backing right-wing Republicans in races that were largely won by Democrats. “I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it, or maybe it would have been much worse without that,” Musk said via videolink at the New York Times Dealbook conference. Musk said his goal was “either the presidency, the House or the Senate be of the other party. That was my actual goal here, which failed by the way.” The Tesla and SpaceX boss sought to extract a lesson from the folly, telling the audience: “It certainly shows that American elections are not just about money.” “Obviously you can put a lot of money into election and have an effect that is relatively minor, and I think that was the case here,” he continued. The midterms weren’t the South Africa-born tech tycoon’s first foray into American elections. Musk spent more than $250 million to help US President Donald Trump return to the White House for his second term and briefly led the 80-year-old Republican’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), before they had a public falling out. They’ve since reconciled and instead of souring on Republican politics, Musk has continued to back Republicans who the president champions. Among the candidates he backed most strongly was Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, with Musk contributing an estimated $220 million to the Republican, only for the race to be won by James Talarico, a 37-year-old Democrat. The headquarters of several of Musk’s companies, including SpaceX and Tesla, are in Austin, Texas. “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money,” Musk said of the elections, adding: “I didn’t put a lot of personal attention into it because I’m focused on building SpaceX, Tesla.” The post Musk says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ for failed US election spending appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: GOKA BET Strengthens Brand Strategy, Signs Obafemi Martins As Brand Ambassador
item.description: Sports betting and gaming company GOKA BET has strengthened its brand positioning with the unveiling of former Super Eagles striker Obafemi Martins as its official brand ambassador, in a strategic move aimed at deepening its connection with sports and entertainment audiences across Nigeria and Africa. The partnership, announced at a press conference held in Lagos, Nigeria, represents a significant step in the company’s efforts to build a distinctive entertainment brand and expand its reach within the African market. Speaking at the event, GOKA BET’s Marketing Manager and Partnership Specialist, Titilayo Ismail Adebanjo, described Martins’ appointment as an important milestone in the company’s growth journey. He said that the former Nigerian international’s remarkable football career, international experience and longstanding relationship with football fans made him a valuable addition to the brand. According to him, the partnership goes beyond securing a familiar face for the company, as it is designed to create meaningful connections with football supporters and entertainment audiences through engaging campaigns, memorable brand experiences and other initiatives. Adebanjo said GOKA BET was committed to building a trusted and distinctive platform anchored on accessibility, reliability, transparency and customer satisfaction. He added that the company recognised the expectations of Nigerian customers and would continue to pursue innovation and improved customer experiences to strengthen public confidence in its services. Speaking on his appointment, Martins expressed excitement about joining the GOKA BET family, describing football as a powerful force that connects people, creates unforgettable moments and brings millions of fans together. The former striker said his experiences playing professional football in different countries had given him a deeper appreciation of the passion the game generates among Nigerian and African supporters. He described the partnership as an opportunity to connect with sports and casino fans in a new and exciting way while contributing to the growth of a brand making its mark in the Nigerian and African markets. “I have played and scored goals across some of the biggest stages in world football, and now I’m bringing that same passion and winning mentality with me on a new journey with GOKA BET,” Martins said. He added that he looked forward to working with the company to develop exciting experiences and engaging campaigns that would strengthen its relationship with football fans across the continent. Martins also called on his supporters and football lovers across Nigeria and Africa to join him on the new journey, expressing optimism about the opportunities ahead. On responsible gaming, both Martins and Adebanjo emphasised the importance of ensuring that betting and casino gaming remained forms of entertainment rather than a guaranteed source of income. item.title: Lagos-Ibadan gridlock: Tinubu’s aide spends five hours in traffic, faults contractor
item.description: President Bola Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Sunday Dare, has faulted the timing of ongoing construction on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after being caught in traffic for more than five hours on his way to Ibadan, Oyo State. Dare lamented that the congestion had left thousands of travellers stranded, forcing some to abandon their vehicles and walk long distances to their destinations. In a Facebook post on Wednesday night, he questioned why the Chinese firm handling the project chose to carry out the work during peak traffic periods instead of at night when fewer vehicles use the road. “It beats me why a Chinese Contractor would choose the busiest hours of vehicular traffic to construct the bridge and road around this exit point. Stranded cars, thousands of people trekking to get home,” he wrote. He added, “What happened to doing construction work during the obituary hours when traffic is lean? This is unnecessary pain. It needs to be corrected.” The traffic disruption followed the recommencement of work on a pedestrian bridge around the Aseese section of the expressway on Wednesday, affecting motorists travelling in both directions. item.title: Taiwo Obe pays tribute to late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: Founder of The Journalism Clinic, Taiwo Obe, has paid tribute to the late Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited, Olufemi Ajasa, recalling their professional relationship and describing his death as a painful loss. Obe, in a tribute shared on social media, recounted how Ajasa participated in one of the first paid journalism training programmes organised at The Hub, the training facility of The Journalism Clinic, in Anifowose, Lagos. He said the training, held around 2015, had three participants from Vanguard’s Online Desk, including then Online Editor, John Abayomi, Adekunle Aliyu and Ajasa. Obe recalled that Vanguard’s Chairman, Sam Amuka-Pemu, had earlier visited the facility and promised that the newspaper would send its staff to training programmes organised there. According to him, Amuka-Pemu fulfilled the promise by ensuring that Vanguard staff participated in the training. Obe traced his relationship with Amuka-Pemu to around 1997, when his company, TaijoWonukabe Limited, moved from an office provided by late columnist Pini Jason Onyegbadue to a three-bedroom bungalow on Bassie Ogamba Street, off Adeniran Ogunsanya, Surulere, Lagos. He said the property belonged to Madam Pemu, a relation of Amuka-Pemu, who lived in a separate bungalow within the same premises. Obe recalled that when Amuka-Pemu visited Madam Pemu shortly after the company moved in, he approached the veteran journalist to introduce himself. “Money is good. See how you boys have changed this building,” Amuka-Pemu reportedly told him after their exchange of pleasantries. Obe said the encounter marked the beginning of a relationship that continued over the years. He added that when Amuka-Pemu visited The Hub shortly after its establishment around 2015, the veteran journalist promised that Vanguard would participate in the facility’s training programmes. Recalling his encounters with Ajasa after the training, Obe described the late journalist as respectful, ambitious and consistently well-dressed. “Since that training, I had encountered Femi in various places and positions. He remained as respectful as ever; always go-getting and consistently impeccably-dressed,” he wrote. Vanguard had reported that Ajasa died at the age of 44 after a brief illness. Expressing grief over his death, Obe concluded his tribute with the Yoruba expression, “Sùn re ò, Femooo,” meaning farewell and rest well. item.title: Fountain of Life crisis: Jimmy Odukoya alleges conspiracy
item.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou The leadership crisis rocking The Fountain of Life Church has taken a fresh turn, with its Senior Pastor, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, breaking his silence on allegations surrounding his leadership, the controversial succession video involving his late father and claims of financial impropriety. Addressing church workers on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, Odukoya gave his account of the prolonged disagreements between him, members of the church’s Board of Trustees (BOT) and his sisters, insisting that he remains the Senior Pastor despite the controversy. The meeting, which reportedly attracted about 300 workers, provided an opportunity for the embattled cleric to explain his position following the circulation of a video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, allegedly indicated a succession preference involving Pastor Kunle Areogun. Odukoya, who arrived at the church premises in a convoy of about five vehicles accompanied by security personnel, entered the auditorium at about 6.45 p.m. and was received with applause by the workers. Speaking emotionally, he said he had endured considerable distress over the crisis but initially chose to remain silent in the hope that the disagreements would be resolved internally. He said the decision by some board members to make his late father’s succession video public compelled him to address the workers and clarify issues surrounding the leadership dispute. Succession video and father’s instruction One of the major issues addressed by Odukoya was the video in which his late father reportedly expressed a preference for Areogun to take over the church’s leadership after his death. He said the recording was made around 2021, shortly before his father travelled to the United States for surgery. According to him, his father, uncertain about the outcome of the medical procedure, decided to document his thoughts on the future leadership of the church. Odukoya said he personally recorded the video, while his late father’s elder brother, John Odukoya, was also aware of the exercise. He, however, admitted that he retained the recording despite his father’s subsequent instruction to delete it after the surgery was successful. “Following my father’s successful surgery, he instructed me to delete the recording because the circumstances that prompted its creation had changed, but I chose to retain the video against my father’s instruction and this I admit as a grave mistake,” he said. He added that only a few people, including his sisters, knew about the recording. The disclosure raises questions about the circumstances surrounding the recording, its intended status after the surgery and the decision to make it public several years later. It also brings into focus the distinction between a succession preference expressed by the late founder and the formal governance processes through which leadership of the church is determined. item.title: Ban sign-out ceremonies at all levels of education, say parents, student leaders
item.description: By Adesina Wahab In recent years, a fad has taken root in Nigeria’s education system, the practice of signing out of school when students conclude their examinations, even without being sure of what the results would look like. It is especially rampant at secondary school and tertiary education levels. Out of what many have labelled youthful exuberance, the graduating students do engage in various activities, including holding wild parties. Read Also: (Video) UNN Party Tragedy: How I regained consciousness, found friends lying lifeless – Survivor In May this year, many parents, guardians and even teachers were left bewildered when the social media was full of videos of some male secondary school students fondling their female counterparts in broad daylight. Some male students were also seen signing on the uniforms of their female colleagues in their private areas. The students were traced to a particular school in Ondo State and punishment meted out to them. But at tertiary education level, wild parties and binge drinking have led to unnecessary deaths. Only in April this year, after the second convocation ceremony of Bamidele Olumilua University of Education, Science and Technology (BOUESTI) in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State, three persons, two of whom were graduating students of the university, died in a stampede that resulted from a fight at a party thrown by some students of the university. A member of staff of the hotel where the party was held was the third casualty. Investigations by the Police revealed that a fight broke out during the party and that sharp objects were freely used, leading to people scampering for safety and many people being trampled upon. Scores of people sustained varying degrees of injuries. Just few days ago, the news broke that some students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, died as a result of what they consumed at a sign-out party organised by some graduating students. The figure initially given was eight but in the end, four students were confirmed dead. Even if it was one person that died, human life is too valuable to be toyed with. Reacting to the development, the Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole. He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country. “I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sing-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others. “This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 19, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened early morning trading on Thursday, November 19, 2026, with diverging trends across the official and informal currency segments, as the official interbank spot market showed mild appreciation while the parallel market maintained pressure above the ₦1,440 threshold. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) placed the US dollar at ₦1,350.50 as of early Thursday morning, reflecting a slight gain of 0.10 percent for the local currency from its early session opening of ₦1,351.81. This follows Wednesday’s official volume-weighted closing benchmark of ₦1,363.23 per dollar published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, also referred to as the black market, Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar within a selling band of ₦1,445 to ₦1,468, with buying rates hovering between ₦1,435 and ₦1,455 depending on transaction volume and location. Following Wednesday’s late trading close where street rates climbed as high as ₦1,453 to ₦1,468, the spread between the official NFEM benchmark and the informal market stands between ₦90 and ₦105 per dollar. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Currency analysts attribute the persistent divergence between both windows to moderating autonomous foreign exchange inflows alongside heightened seasonal import demand and corporate obligations. Market data indicates that weekly inflows into the foreign exchange market recently moderated to $807.6 million as offshore portfolio investors adopted a cautious stance. Despite recent liquidity interventions by the apex bank—which have trimmed Nigeria’s external reserves by approximately $390 million from their late-October peak of $55.26 billion—the country’s reserve buffer remains over 26 percent higher than the $43.54 billion recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. Financial institutions expect the Central Bank of Nigeria to sustain targeted liquidity support to keep official NFEM rates anchored within the ₦1,350 to ₦1,365 band, even as unfulfilled retail demand continues to drive premiums in the parallel segment. item.title: American strategist denies receiving $4.5m for Tinubu interview
item.description: By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government for her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu. London, in a post on her X account on Wednesday night, described the allegation as a smear campaign, insisting that neither the Nigerian government nor anyone else in the country paid her the reported sum. She said her visit to Nigeria was to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to see the country for herself. “I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million. I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself. “This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she wrote. The denial comes amid controversy surrounding her interview with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday, and reports alleging that she was linked to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government in the United States. Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar had called on the Presidency to clarify whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying contract and disclose the details of the arrangement. In a statement issued on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal. He said the filings indicated that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but maintained that the Presidency should clarify whether the interview formed part of the contract. Atiku demanded the publication of the contract, details of the payment and the release of the full, unedited recording of the interview. He also questioned the nature of the engagement, arguing that the Presidency should establish whether the encounter was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement. The former vice president further asked the government to disclose who authorised the payment, the source of the funds and whether public money was involved. The controversy followed London’s earlier social media posts praising the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States under Tinubu and US President Donald Trump. In one of the posts, she described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, saying the security cooperation between both countries was producing results and could create further economic and trade opportunities. She also expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria in efforts to strengthen relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government. item.title: South-South: Incumbents, heavyweights in make or mar gov battles
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume WITH the 2027 general elections approaching, the battle for four governorship seats across the South-South is gathering momentum, with incumbents, political heavyweights and emerging contenders positioning themselves for control of the region’s political landscape. In Akwa Ibom, Governor Umo Eno is banking on his performance, incumbency and the mass defection of Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, members to the All Progressives Congress, APC, to secure a second term. In Cross River, Governor Bassey Otu enjoys the advantages of incumbency, federal backing and expanding political alliances, but faces a determined challenge from PDP’s Arthur Jarvis Archibong. Rivers presents a more complicated contest, with the influence of FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, the political grievances arising from the protracted power struggle in the state and the growing appeal of opposition parties shaping the calculations. In Delta, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori appears to enjoy an advantageous position following his defection to the APC and the support of influential political leaders, while opposition candidates seek to exploit the changing political alignments. Across the four states, the contests will test the strength of incumbency, party structures, political alliances, grassroots mobilisation and the capacity of opposition candidates to convert public support into electoral victories. There will be no governorship polls in Bayelsa and Edo. Eno holds ace as opposition plots upset in Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno of the APC appears to have the upper hand in the battle for Akwa Ibom Government House, facing former senator and minister, John Akpanudoedehe of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and former House of Representatives member, Michael Enyong of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC. Eno, who hails from Akwa Ibom North-East Senatorial District, Uyo, enjoys the advantage of incumbency and the political boost arising from the defection of several PDP members to the APC. His performance in office over the last three and a half years is also being projected as a major selling point as he seeks another four years. Although Akpanudoedehe commands considerable political recognition in the state, and Enyong brings legislative experience to the contest, observers believe the incumbent’s political machinery and expanding support base could prove difficult to dislodge. A public affairs analyst, Mr Ben Ikoriko, believes Eno’s empowerment programmes, particularly for people at the lower end of the state’s economy, could secure him substantial electoral support. item.title: Tompolo’s N3.6bn fleet raises questions
item.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, which safeguards some of the nation’s critical oil and gas assets, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has donated over 600 vehicles estimated at about N3.68 billion to support the re-election campaign of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu across states. Tompolo, a former militant leader, doubles as the Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, a group mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election. Daily Trust reports that the cost of the vehicles has exceeded the N500 million individual donation limit under the Electoral Act 2026, but the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says the question of whether non-cash donations are covered by the law may require judicial interpretation. The vehicles constitute a series of donations committed to supporting President Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. Gov Sani flags off five roads in Kaduna communities Adebutu’s return to ballot signals APC’s defeat in Ogun – PDP scribe There have also been pledges, including a promise of N10 million reward to each ward councilor in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) by the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike. The proposed reward would amount to N620 million if all 62 councillors deliver their respective wards. The material donations have renewed concerns among observers over compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act on campaign spending limits. Section 92(8) of the act provides that an individual or other entity shall not donate more than N500 million to a candidate. Under subsection (9), a candidate who knowingly contravenes the provision is liable, upon conviction, to a fine of one per cent of the permitted campaign expenditure limit, imprisonment for up to 12 months, or both. An individual who knowingly exceeds the donation limit is liable to a fine of five times the excess amount under subsection (10). Although there is no public evidence to show that Tompolo has donated sums above the N500m threshold to the Tinubu campaign, media reports revealed that he has so far distributed about 633 vehicles across at least 21 states through PBAT Door-to-Door Movement. The vehicles comprise 583 Opel Zafira wagons and 50 Sharon, with a combined market value estimated at N3.68 billion, based on average prices of fairly used vehicles of the respective models. The donations have raised questions about compliance with the electoral law and attempts by individuals to circumvent it by opting for non-cash donations. item.title: Govt of the day serving interests of few – Ndume
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Senator representing Borno South Senatorial District, Ali Ndume, Wednesday, admitted being part of the country’s political failure, saying government of the day is a government of some people, by some people and for some people. Ndume also lamented rising political violence in the country, saying anyone found sponsoring such acts should be held responsible. Speaking on Prime Time, an Arise Television programme, he expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which public office holders were amassing wealth, saying many of them were gluttons. He said: “I am part of the failure, I cannot deny that. I am not going to claim to be the best or better than anybody. But if I had known that this is how this politics is going to turn out to be, I wouldn’t have joined it. You can compare politics to AIDS. Once you catch it, you can’t say you don’t have AIDS. I’m telling you. It’s a dangerous game, especially in Nigeria. You can’t get cured. “It’s true that government of the day has been a government of some people, by some people and for some people. If it were a government of all, this complaint and all that would not be happening. It did not start with this government. It started with the previous government. It has become a practice that you must be within the cycle. Even within the cycle, there are cabals running the government.” On violence as a tool for political competition, he said: “In fact, that is why I am happy that everybody is concerned, so that we may nip it in the bud. My friend and colleague, Ningi, moved the motion after we spoke, and I seconded the motion. Then you can see how our colleagues showed concern, and Nigerians generally. It is one of the motions that was apolitical because the problem is like fire. If it catches, you don’t know when it will stop, and you may have a problem putting it off. “It has also happened in a few countries where things got out of hand and, in extreme cases, reached a stage where the country’s government collapsed. You could see what happened in Bangladesh. Some years back, you could hear what happened in the Middle East. “When people easily take the law into their own hands to express their hunger and use whatever is available that can be regarded as a weapon or tool, then it becomes a dangerous thing.” Vanguard News The post Govt of the day serving interests of few – Ndume appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Anchor Borrowers Scheme: Reps divided over calls to write off farmers’ N1trn loans waiver
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina Abuja — A motion seeking the cancellation of outstanding loans obtained by farmers under various government-backed agricultural intervention programmes yesterday divided members of the House of Representatives. Lawmakers disagreed over whether distressed farmers should be granted debt relief or subjected to an investigation. The motion, sponsored by Inuwa Garba, representing Yamaltu/Deba federal constituency of Gombe State, was predicated on the economic difficulties confronting farmers, particularly the impact of insecurity, climate change, natural disasters and other challenges that had disrupted agricultural production across the country. The federal government had, in recent years, introduced several agricultural financing initiatives, including the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme, Commercial Agriculture Credit Scheme and NIRSAL-supported facilities, to boost food production, empower farmers and strengthen national food security. Leading debate on the motion, Garba said insecurity, banditry, insurgency, farmer-herder clashes, flooding, drought and other environmental challenges had significantly undermined agricultural activities, resulting in crop failures, loss of investments and reduced farm incomes. He argued that many beneficiaries of government-sponsored agricultural loans were unable to meet their repayment obligations, not because they were unwilling to repay, but because circumstances beyond their control had severely affected their productive capacity and financial stability. According to him, continued accumulation and enforcement of outstanding debts, including principal, interest and penalties, can push already struggling farmers further into poverty, expose them to asset seizures and discourage participation in future agricultural activities. However, opposing the proposed debt cancellation, Bamidele Salam, representing Ede South/Ede North/Ejigbo/Egbedore federal constituency of Osun State, questioned the justification for a blanket waiver, citing findings in the Auditor-General for the Federation’s report before the House. Salam, who chairs the House Committee on Public Accounts, alleged that some beneficiaries of agricultural intervention loans running into over N1tn diverted the funds to businesses and personal investments. unrelated to farming. He said some beneficiaries who approached the Central Bank of Nigeria and commercial banks for agricultural loans allegedly channelled the funds into real estate acquisitions in Abuja, Lagos and even Dubai. He also expressed concern over the state of the Bank of Agriculture which, he said, had been rendered virtually immobile by N795billion in loans owed by beneficiaries, many of whom allegedly diverted the funds. Salam warned that approving a blanket waiver without establishing how the loans were utilised would set a dangerous precedent for future government intervention programmes. item.title: FAAC disburses N2.4trn to FG, states, LGs in October
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief ABUJA — THE Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, yesterday, shared the sum of N2.441 trillion among the three tiers of government. The amount was from the October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, which was shared at the FAAC meeting held in Abuja on Wednesday. The N2.441 trillion comprised distributable statutory revenue of N1.688 trillion and Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N752.488 billion. A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, indicated that gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available in the month of October 2026. Total deduction for cost of collection was N128.797 billion while total transfers, refunds and savings stood at N1.241 trillion. According to the communiqué sent by Director of Press of the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, Bawa Mokwa, gross statutory revenue of N2.999 trillion was received for the month of October 2026. This was lower than the sum of N3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by N97.323 billion. Gross revenue of N812.446 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in October 2026. This was lower than the N816.872 billion available in the month of September 2026 by N4.426 billion. The communiqué stated that from the N2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of N856.065 billion and the state governments received a total sum of N809.909 billion. The Local Government Councils received N568.701 billion, while the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue. On the N1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the Federal Government received N780.816 billion and the State Governments received N396.040 billion. The Local Government Councils received N305.331 billion and the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue. From the N752.488 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, the State Governments received N413.868 billion and the Local Government Councils received N263.371 billion. In October 2026, Excise Duty and CET Levies increased marginally, while Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, and Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue all decreased. Vanguard News The post FAAC disburses N2.4trn to FG, states, LGs in October appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: State police on verge of reality; operational guidelines bill submitted to Justice Ministry
item.description: By Henry Umoru & Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Operation of State police in Nigeria is at the verge of being realised. The National Assembly yesterday transmitted the bill ratified by the 36 state houses of Assembly to President Bola Tinubu yesterday for assent. The lawmakers asked the president to send a bill on the operational guidelines for state police for passage. Chief of Staff to president, Femi Gbajabiamila disclosed yesterday that the operational guidelines bill has been forwarded to the Ministry of Justice for validation. To quicken the process, the Senate asked President Tinubu to forward to the National Assembly the National Policing Bill which would provide for the operationlisation of state police across the 36 states of the federation for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage. It also mandated the clerk to the National Assembly, CNA, Kamoru Ogunlana to transmit the constitutional amendment bill that seeks to establish State Police Services in Nigeria to the President for assent, having satisfied all the constitutional requirements, in line with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004. President Tinubu, however, received the State Police Bill later yesterday, with the Chief of Staff to the President, Mr, Femi Gbajabiamila, saying the bill requested by the Senate had been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation. According to him, upon receipt of the validated version, the President Working Group, which he chairs, will review and present it, alongside its report to the President for consideration. Resolutions of the Senate were sequel to a motion, titled “Passage of Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 and sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele. Bamidele, who urged the President to forward to the Senate expeditiously the National Policing Bill, said in his presentation: “The Senate: Recall that pursuant to Section 9(1) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, the National Assembly processed an Executive Bill seeking to alter the provisions of the Constitution to establish State Police as part of the national policing structure. “Also recall that the Senate and the House of Representatives on June 24 and July, 23, 2026, respectively, overwhelmingly supported the bill with over 2/3 majority votes, thereby meeting the constitutional threshold for the passage of the bill by the National Assembly; “Aware that the National Assembly transmitted the bill to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for the mandatory approval by resolution of not less than 2/3 majority of the State Houses of Assembly as provided by Section 9(2) of the Constitution before the Bill can be passed; The states… “Also aware that the 36 State Houses of Assembly have transmitted their resolution of the bill to the National Assembly, namely Abia, Adamawa, Anambra, Akwa-Ibom, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Benue, Borno, Cross-River, Delta, Ebonyi, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Im

item.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. His nomination puts him on course to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as his party prepares to reverse Republican policies and investigate the administration. Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3, when he would become the first Black politician to hold the powerful post. With a large Democratic majority, this is seen as something of a formality. Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics. Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination “by acclamation” — without a formal ballot — as some allies had hoped. He argued that every Democrat should have an opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018. The ballot remained secret, with the overall tally made public but individual votes kept anonymous. Ahead of the election, Jeffries met progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare, with proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage among the topics discussed. The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party’s plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs. “Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters Tuesday. “We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.” – Brooklyn roots – Raised in Brooklyn’s working-class Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012. Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022. He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump’s first impeachment trial in 2020. As speaker, Jeffries would preside over one of Washington’s most powerful institutions and stand second in line to the presidency behind the vice president.
